subject: Re: MAP: Deployment mode & region decision — AtlasHealth evaluation plan
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation plan + MAP — deployment guidance needed

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. We need to lock down our mutual action plan so we can run the evaluation and decide whether to go Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. Key constraints:
- PHI data will be processed for a subset of flows (encrypted at rest, strict audit logging)
- Initial target region: US East (low latency) but we may require EU later for cross-border data
- Timeline: pilot evaluation in June, procurement by end of July

Can you share a MAP draft with milestones and the recommended deployment modes for each stage? Also, please include any security evidence (SOC 2, KMS options) we should expect. I'll loop in procurement (procure@atlashealth.com) once we have costs for Dedicated/Private.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director of Product
AtlasHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan + MAP — deployment guidance needed

Elena —

Appreciate the clear constraints. I've attached a first-pass MAP (atlas_map_draft.xlsx) and a high-level SOC2/ evidence checklist. Quick proposal:

Phase A — Hosted PoC (2 weeks):
- Region: US East (low-latency hosted nodes)
- Goal: functional validation, end-to-end instrumentation, and initial quality checks
- Why Hosted: fastest time-to-value; no infra commitment for the first evaluation

Phase B — Dedicated Pilot (4–6 weeks):
- Region: US East dedicated pool; reserved capacity with predictable QPS for threshold testing
- Goal: throughput/latency SLOs under simulated production load and KV cache behavior
- Why Dedicated: predictable performance for production and easier SLA negotiation

Phase C — Private / On-prem (optional, procurement-led):
- For customers requiring air-gapped or customer-managed networks (costly and longer lead times)

I've copied Priyom (solutions/infra) for technical feasibility and to include a short evaluation checklist for deployment acceptance criteria (KV cache, quantization profile, KMS integration). We can toggle the order (e.g., run Hosted PoC then move to Dedicated) if you want to minimize ramp time.

Attachments: atlas_map_draft.xlsx, soc2_evidence_checklist.pdf

Next steps: please confirm if the Hosted-first approach works for you and whether procurement needs an early estimate for Dedicated/Private to start internal approvals. I'll update the MAP with ownership and dates once we lock the approach.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan + MAP — deployment guidance needed

Elena / Marissa —

Technical notes from infra/solutions side:
- Hosted PoC in us-east: trivial to stand up. For PHI, we recommend TLS+customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for token encryption at rest — we can support KMS integrations (AWS KMS or customer HSM).
- Performance: if you anticipate >10k concurrent active sessions for the primary flow, Dedicated will be the right path for predictable latency; otherwise Hosted with intelligent batching and prefix caching will be cost-effective.
- KV cache warm-up: allow 24–48 hours for realistic token-cache hit-rate testing. Include this in the MAP ramp period.
- Compliance evidence: attached "security-q-answers.docx" with brief responses; for deeper audit we can provide scoped SOC2 artifacts under an NDA.

I'll prepare a short tech acceptance checklist to append to the MAP (model quantization profile to use for ramp, target 95th percentile SLOs, test dataset pointers).

—Priyom
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Priyom —

Thanks for the draft MAP and notes. Procurement asked whether we can run a Hosted PoC in US East for two weeks first before committing to Dedicated — their ask is to see latency/quality on our real traffic (anonymized) and then move to Dedicated only if key metrics require it. A few procurement questions:
- Can you provide a rough Dedicated pricing range (monthly reserve vs on-demand) for the pilot config?
- If we later convert to Private, what are typical lead times and biggest blockers (network, EHS, audits)?

I'll confirm the anonymized dataset and timeline (aiming to start Hosted PoC week of Jun 23). If procurement needs a figure to circulate internally I can provide the Hosted-first approach but they want a Dedicated ballpark too.

Best,
Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>, procure@atlashealth.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan + MAP — deployment guidance needed

Elena —

Hosted-first is reasonable and aligns with our recommended flow. Quick answers for procurement:
- Dedicated pilot estimate (US East, small reserved pool for 4–6 weeks): ballpark $18k–$28k/month depending on instance mix and guaranteed throughput. On-demand burst pricing will be +30% above reserve. I'll have Sean (finance/sales ops) provide a tighter quote and a simple procurement worksheet.
- Private/on-prem: typical lead time is 8–12 weeks from PO (network setup, install, and compliance scoping). Biggest blockers: on-prem networking (firewalls, NATs), customer KMS access for BYOK, and SOC2 scoping for locally-hosted evidence.

Action items I'll update in the MAP (and attach final versions to the HubSpot record):
- Marissa: update MAP milestones + owner assignment + close target 2025-07-31
- Priyom: finalize tech acceptance checklist and quantization profile by Jun 18
- Sean: dedicated pricing worksheet by EOD Jun 13
- Elena: confirm anonymized dataset and confirm Hosted PoC start week of Jun 23

I've uploaded the MAP and security checklist to Drive and created a DocuSign for the initial PoC addendum (link above). Once procurement has the Dedicated ballpark from Sean I'll include it in the MAP and share the updated file.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: atlas_map_draft.xlsx, soc2_evidence_checklist.pdf, security-q-answers.docx
